زَحْمٌ [originally an inf. n.,] i. q. قَوْمٌ مُزْدَحِمُونَ [A party, or company of men, straitening one another by pressure; pushing, pressing, crowding, or thronging, one another; i. e. a press, crowd, or throng]. (K, * TA.) A poet says, “↓ جَآءَ بِزَحْمٍ مَعَ زَحْمٍ فَٱزْدَحَمْ
المَوْجِ إِذَا المَوْجُ ٱلْتَطَمْ ↓ تَزَاحُمَ
” [He brought a crowd with a crowd, and they pressed, one against another, like the dashing together of the waves when the waves beat one another]: he uses [here] an inf. n. not conformable to the verb. (ISd, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
